a.xlink:title: The ability to repeat an experimental procedure and obtain results consistent with declared criteria when its inputs, environment, randomness, and execution conditions are specified.

A reproducible specification of workload, measurement boundary, run rules, and comparison procedure that lets results from different systems be compared and lets a system be judged against a baseline.
Identifying the exact model, code, data, configuration, and dependencies in an execution or release.
The software packages, versions, native libraries, and runtime configuration on which an execution depends.
Recording immutable, addressable versions of datasets so that a training run or evaluation can identify exactly which data it used.
Recording each run's code, data, configuration, metrics, and artifacts in a queryable store for comparison and reproduction.
Treating model, feature, and pipeline configuration as versioned, reviewed, and tested code.
Preserving retired models, data references, and evaluation records needed for audit, reproduction, or rollback after service ends.
Run-to-run variation in floating-point results because non-associative reductions change order with atomics, kernel selection, parallel layout, batch composition, or hardware.
A kernel property that each request's output is bitwise independent of batch size and co-batched requests, one way to remove a source of run-to-run numerical variation in serving.
Packaging a model, its code, and its dependencies as an immutable image that runs unchanged across machines, leaving the scheduling of those containers across a cluster to the cluster manager.

Randomizing the order in which training examples are visited, by a full permutation or an approximate buffered shuffle over sharded files, trading the randomness that stochastic optimization assumes against the sequential reads that storage delivers cheaply.
